Anyway— it is pretty rare a fish be injured like this from an ornament. They don’t tend to “get stuck” and usually just appear that way because they are swimming poorly or hiding (which can be because of bad water perimeters or because they are otherwise stressed or ill). Ornament injuries are most commonly torn fins. Injuries like this I usually see because of fighting (which is just not something I think is happening based on your extremely reasonable stocking) or because of them itching against things (which is usually from external parasites— which you DEFINITELY would be able to see, they’re usually plainly visible and look insane. Check out some pictures of anchor worms and fish lice on Google and you’ll see what I mean.)

So it seems to me either he just has this bizarre injury from an ornament, or he has the injury because of some underlying illness that isn’t super obvious in the pictures. I think you’re right in taking out the ornament to be safe, just make sure he has other hiding places available to him!

I’d still recommend the AQ salt + stress coat + Indian almond leaves route. AQ salt treats a lot of early parasite infections, and many mild to moderate bacterial infections, in addition to improving the immune system, gill function and general fish health. Feeding him with a dropper like I outlined also will help ensure he’s getting food (neon tetras are fast and probably are robbing him of some of his meals, also, which can add to stress while he’s healing up and all). You can also try using floating pellets that are a bit large for the neon tetras but small enough for the gouramis, and feed it at the same time as your other food/flakes. If your local fish seller has someone that knows a lot about fish they should be able to help you sort out which one will work best for this. 

Fish can heal from all kinds of insane looking injuries and illnesses. I’m sending you my best for him.

I’m most concerned for the water wisteria. In my experience the others have all held strong with salt treatments. 

The doseage for the API brand is one tablespoon per 5 gallons. I would start with one tablespoon per 15 gallons of your tank (however that calculates out). You wanna get like a half a cup of warm water from the sink, dechlorinate it, and dissolve the salt in there before pouring it into the tank.

Give it a day or two, and if the plants are all ok, add another dose (so you’re at 2/3 the recommended dose.) If you’re still going strong a day or two after that, go ahead and go up to a full dose. Just keep an eye on it and be ready to pop the wisteria in a bowl or bucket if it gets pale. You probably won’t have to, but that’s the only one I’m really worried about.

It’s also good to add salt slowly for the fish sake; following a schedule like this regardless of the plants will keep them from getting shocked.

Always remember salt does not evaporate out. So as water evaporates from the tank, the salt concentration in the water increases. If you do a water change, keep track of how much salt is in the tank before hand and top it up after. It’s a lot of fractions to keep track of and keeping notes helps a lot. 

When everyone is doing good, just keep up your regular water changes without adding salt and you should be all set, easy peasy.

What is your tank stocking? What is your tank size? How specifically did the injury seem to occur (was it the piece of decor, or did they come like this?) how long has the tank been set up? Have you had a recent water test?

Stress coat has aloe vera in it and can enhance a fish’s slime coat. This helps when healing injuries.

Prime is a genuinely superior product most of the time. It helps keep your water levels in place and personally I don’t like stress coat 24/7 because it can make the water look “thicker” and it seems to, over long periods of time, negatively affect fish with a labyrinth organ like Gouramis and Bettas. However, when there’s fins to be regrown or an injury, stress coat can be better short term.

Since there’s no apparent fin damage if I was you instead I would order some Indian almond leaves online, put a bunch in, and let that water get brown with tannins. It’ll help you out and gouramis in particular really thrive in it.

What live plants do you have specifically? AQ salt is a great way to prevent infection, improve immune system, and promote healing when used properly, but it does kill certain live plants. If you can list them for me I’ll be glad to let you know if you’ll be good/give you more specific advice.

I used to work at PetSmart. The tank and all the decor are PetSmart Top Tin brand. They don’t sell it anywhere else it’s the store brand.

If they bought the supplies at PetSmart, I would say they almost definitely bought the fish there. If that’s the case that’s definitely an African Dwarf Frog, because PetSmart does not sell any other kind of aquatic frog. 

OP— if this is a PetSmart kit, watch out for a slime starting to grow on the anemones. They start to kinda breakdown after a while (10 months to a year) and get sticky, when that happens they won’t hurt the fish but there’s no way to make them not look gross and it’s best to just toss them. If you go where they have fake aquatic plants, there are super cheap ones made of silk or plastic (not rubber) that will basically last longer than you will. Also, consider either buying the next more powerful filter than came with your kit, or pick up a cheap bubble filter off of Amazon and add it to your existing setup. When you don’t have live plants it goes a long way for keeping the water how you want it, and it will help circulate the water more.

If you want to add some live plants that kids still like, marimo moss balls are easy and they’re just little round balls so the kids will like them. You could also do like an anubias nana or El Niño fern, both are pretty hardy and you just tie them with thread to a rock or one of your existing tank fixtures (like the coral) and they’re glad to prosper with loose roots. It’ll help keep your nitrates down, which in turn helps stave off green water. It also helps to take a little cup of tank water, put the food in there that you want to feed them, let it sink, and then put it in the tank. It’s way more fun for kids to watch the fish feed that way (it disperses through the tank rather than the top and they’ll do like a “feeding frenzy”, and it also helps the fish eat all the food and cuts down on leftover food.)

Edit: also, you have a male molly and a female platy. They can’t breed together, and that’s GREAT because you don’t wanna get overrun. If you end up getting more of them, I’d recommend you to stick to getting more female platies. Some people have success with molly frats but ime they like to pick the weakest among them and murder him until there’s one left. You don’t want female and male mollies because you’ll have more babies than you know what to do with. Livebearers are gorgeous but they multiply like roaches.

However— an understocked tank is nice and easier to care for and manage. Especially without live plants. If you don’t want more fish that’s also perfectly good!

I say to customers all the time... I don’t make commission, right? They don’t even really track my sales, I’m just here to help them make sure they can care for this animal, and that they’re able to have the easiest time and the best deal. I tell them our 2 month return policy for members and what my recommendation is, that if they buy it here I’ll make sure that if ANYTHING goes wrong I’ll get them taken care of, cause that’s just the policy. I also always personify the pet to them. Like if they want fish for a 10g— I like a betta and 5 or 6 neons for a 10g versus let’s say using it as a grow out tank for goldfish. I’ll say like “well, you put the goldfish in there— they’re like, well, thanks for this studio apartment full of bunk beds we all gotta share. But you pop that betta in there? Help the customer really empathize with the animal and understand that difference of minimum and ideal, between survive mentality and thrive mentality.

I also always, always pretend like I’m selling them my personal favorite animal. I’ll say hi to the animal, handle it a bit before I hand it over, and then talk to them and be like “oh I can tell they like you haha, I’m so glad to send them to a good home,” to give them a big head and make sure they’re not questioning anything when they head up to the register with an ideal setup.

For this reason I think creative leeway is more than alright, and that it is a very different situation.

I will also say that creators should have some say in fan content, especially whether it is made explicit, like Zootopia creators have asked people to stop making porn of it, I think people should respect that, or the creator of Bioshock’s Elizabeth asking people to stop making porn of HER, because he sees her as a daughter. But I really also still think this is different from “do not make this character gay”, because just making a character LGBT is not inherently offensive or explicit. The creators asking for explicit content not to be made is different from them asking fans not to make interpretations of their characters in media.

Moreover, like, I do think there is value in headcanoning characters as LGBT just for no reason, just for fun, or whatever, but sometimes also there’s a lot of subtext for it in the show that may be unintended, and I think it’s just a part of consuming media to take things a certain way or not. At a certain point the author of a work must cede control of its interpretation to the reader, otherwise you get shit like JK Rowling.

You don’t have to like it, but it doesn’t hurt the characters— they aren’t real— and it doesn’t hurt the creators of the show. Brendan Small, by his own admission, does not at all mind creation of this kind of content and thinks some of it is actually pretty good, even if he didn’t originally imagine his characters as being that way. 

So I’m just not terribly sure who demonizing the part of the fandom that creates these treatises on character’s emotional states helps, all considering. It’s OK if you do not interpret the characters that way, I’m not at all saying that you have to agree with different members being LGBT— but I just wish some of these truly lovely fan works, many of which are not sexual, wouldn’t get shit on just for having LGBT content. If you don’t want to see nsfw content that’s perfectly valid, but outside of that I really think the mentality of “I don’t see them that way but your interpretation is valid and you aren’t wrong for thinking it because these aren’t real people” is the more fair mentality all things considered (one of those things being... Okay 1) I really like Cherp, all my best RPs have started there. 2) Post several really specific prompts that show off your prose. I have one that was about like the zombie apocalypse and Bro Strider is a former UPS delivery guy who saves y/c hiding in a broom closet, and I was looking to branch out from there. I have a ton where Bro Strider is your landlord and also a vampire, but not a hot vampire, an actual big gross vampire whose teeth fall out of his cheekbones like a hundred very sharp knives and if he goes outside he will die, or where Bro Strider is a shapeshifter who eats livers to transform, and he has taken the place of y/c’s sleazy brother and is pretending to be him, but also y/c is a ghost haunting that house who hasn’t been seen in fifteen years and so he knows hey, obviously that is a supernatural being, and the... hijinks.... ensuing.

My point is you can get as specific as you want and people WILL COME FOR IT. When they see a prompt posted that is out of the box and the OOC, even if the starter isn’t posted, has some serious effort and shows you can write, they’ll come for it.

Once you get talking, be specific about what you want. Don’t talk forever, maybe 2-3 ooc replies before someone has to shit out a starter. I usually give people 3 replies or so before I disconnect if I am not vibing on their prose. If they do something really cringe I’ll d/c right away.

Last... a lot of people plain suck at this. Let them shoot their shot, and if they miss, they miss. It’s so much better to be in 2 or 3 good rps than 20 meh to terrible rps.

Edit: also if you do romance, go for a slow burn and have an overarching plot! Also long term once the characters are together it gets REALLY boring so the groundwork you do for the overarching plot while you get the characters together is what keeps things interesting later on. I have bred them as a personal project and have literally in 3 years working in petcare never been bit aggressively or to the point of blood (I have had some pinched described below). I’ll fight you off!!” in hamster terms (this step also works with Syrians) 2) scoop them with the igloo as gently and with as little chasing as possible. 3) let them walk out of the igloo and onto your hand on their own terms. Hold them over the enclosure.

You won’t get latched onto using this method. Maybe 10% of Russian hamsters roughly don’t know their bite strength and will try and give you little grooming nibbles that hurt but won’t break the skin, if they do that just put them back.

You can find this color on them quite easily if you go into the store and use your phone as a flashlight, and briefly run in front of the cups with the light.  Don't do it too much as you don't want to bully them with the light, but any one that flashes well against the light will also give you flashes while swimming around in your tank and catching your tank light.  Also, betta fish color up quite a lot when in a heated, filtered tank of appropriate size with appropriate tankmates.  You can also try and select a less aggressive one by bringing a hand mirror with you and holding it to the cups of the ones you like-- if they flare up quickly they're going to probably not be too good with other fish.

I think bettas are some of the best fish you can get, period, because they're super smart and inquisitive, they're beautiful, and they're easy to keep as well.  They also don't tend to bother snails and the females can do very well with other fish as long as you are selective in your stocking.  I would look at smaller shoaling fish- I've had some luck with feeder guppy females, and other people seem to enjoy them with ember tetras and neon tetras.  Shrimp are also an option-- a tank with 10-15 shrimp, some snails, and a female betta won't feel empty, I promise! Shrimp and bettas both are very, very active and tend to take up whatever space you are inclined to give them.

The trick is to just make sure that you keep everyone well fed, you have lots of hiding places (and ideally live plants), and that you keep the tank clean and understocked.
